title: Graph Neural Networks

children.title: GNN Foundations: Architectures, Convolution, and Message Passing
Surveys and Overviews of GNN Foundations and Representation Learning
children.rationale: These papers provide broad coverage of GNN architectures, tasks, and representation learning, serving as entry points and taxonomies for the field.

children.title: Spectral Graph Convolution and Signal-Processing Foundations
children.rationale: These papers ground graph convolution in spectral theory, signal processing (GSP), and filter design (polynomial, ARMA), establishing the mathematical basis for convolutional operations on graphs.

children.title: Architectural Innovations: Layers, Multi-scale, and Structural Graph CNNs
Layer-Level Architectural Components: Convolutional, Pooling, and Structural Graph CNN Layers
children.rationale: These papers focus on the fundamental design of individual CNN-style layers (convolution, pooling, fully-connected) adapted for graphs, including how to extract locally connected regions, represent graphs as image-like structures, and formulate edge-aware layer operations.

children.title: Multi-scale, Multi-path, and Heterogeneous Graph CNN Architectures
children.rationale: These papers address higher-order architectural challenges—typed/heterogeneous node and edge representations, multi-path aggregation to combat over-smoothing and vanishing gradients, and graph transformer networks that dynamically generate new graph structures—all of which presuppose basic layer designs and extend them to richer structural settings.

These papers propose concrete architectural extensions—new layer types, multipath aggregation, typed nodes, graph transformers, heterogeneous path-integral convolution, and image-based graph representations—that address limitations of vanilla graph convolution.
These papers establish the core GNN paradigms—spectral and spatial graph convolution, message-passing frameworks, surveys, and foundational architectures—that underpin all downstream work.

children.title: Graph Pooling Methods for Graph-Level Representation
Flat and Global Pooling Methods
Basic Global Aggregation Pooling: Sum, Mean, Max, and Empirical Comparisons
children.rationale: These papers focus on straightforward global readout strategies and empirical benchmarking of flat pooling methods across GNN architectures, establishing baseline understanding of how simple aggregations perform on graph classification tasks.

children.title: Advanced Global Pooling: Second-Order Statistics and Attention-Based Multiset Pooling
children.rationale: These papers propose more expressive global pooling mechanisms—second-order covariance pooling and graph multiset transformer pooling—that go beyond simple aggregations to capture richer structural and statistical information from all node representations.
These papers propose or evaluate pooling methods that aggregate all node representations into a single graph-level vector in one step, without hierarchical graph coarsening.

children.title: Hierarchical and Attention-Based Pooling Methods
children.rationale: These papers develop pooling methods that progressively coarsen the graph structure or use attention mechanisms to select and aggregate nodes across multiple levels of granularity.

children.title: Theoretically Expressive and Representation-Power-Oriented Pooling
children.rationale: These papers ground pooling design in formal expressiveness theory (e.g., beyond Weisfeiler-Lehman, exchangeability, isomorphism), aiming to maximize the representational power of graph-level embeddings.

These papers specifically address the problem of aggregating node representations into a single graph-level embedding, proposing and evaluating diverse pooling strategies (hierarchical, attention-based, second-order, spectral, function-space).

children.title: Structural Extensions: Node Features, Graph Geometry, and Beyond Message Passing
Enriching Node and Edge Feature Representations in GNNs
children.rationale: These papers focus on jointly learning or co-embedding node and edge features, or dynamically adapting graph structure to node features, staying within the standard GNN/MPNN pipeline but enriching what is represented.

children.title: Structural and Geometric Inductive Biases: Degree, Dimensionality, and Graph Geometry
children.rationale: These papers address structural limitations of standard aggregation by introducing geometric embeddings, degree-specific convolutions, multi-dimensional/multi-relational graphs, and 2-D graph convolution to better capture neighborhood structure and long-range dependencies.

children.title: Beyond Message Passing: Sheaf Laplacians, Graph Kernels, and Alternative Propagation Frameworks
children.rationale: These papers move beyond the standard MPNN/WL framework by grounding GNNs in alternative mathematical structures—sheaf theory and graph kernels—to overcome expressivity ceilings and enable richer relational modeling.

These papers extend standard GNNs by incorporating geometric structure, multi-dimensional or heterogeneous graphs, co-embedding of edges and nodes, dynamic graph learning, sheaf Laplacians, and kernel-based expressivity—addressing fundamental limitations of vanilla message passing.

rationale: The corpus naturally partitions into foundational GNN architectures and convolution designs, graph pooling methods for graph-level representation, and structural/theoretical extensions that push beyond standard message-passing, reflecting the core methodological progression in the GNN literature.
